title: Hyp Rational Perf
objective: Accelerate rational torsion and saturation through batched reductions and exact checks, retaining replayable certificate boundaries.

handoff.summary: Added bounded prepared reduction of rational genus-2/3 Mumford bases at many good primes, canonical exact fingerprints, shared reduction caches for torsion and saturation, batched finite-field factor stripping, exact auxiliary-prime division filters, cancellation checks, and replayable version-2 saturation certificates. The exact basis-reduction benchmark improves from 0.499-0.540 seconds to 0.178-0.184 seconds (2.77x-3.02x), and saturation reuses two residue-prime reductions across three saturation primes instead of making six provider calls. Focused genus-2/3 tests pass, including exact certificate replay and resource bounds.
risks: This lane accelerates reduction orchestration but does not yet provide the Phase-6 FLINT-backed rational Cantor composition/reduction boundary; Magma remains substantially faster on its comparable finite-Jacobian batch workload.
Auxiliary-prime division filters reduce expensive exact QQ scalar tests, but candidate enumeration dominates larger boxes and can erase the wall-clock gain.
The focused test file is intentionally within this lane, but registering it in the shared node-test manifest is an integration-lane change outside the contract claims.
Prepared finite-field scalar batching activates by feature detection once the Cantor-core lane is integrated; this isolated branch exercises the exact reference fallback.
Validation was performed on linux-x64; required cross-platform validation remains an integration responsibility.
next_steps: Create a narrow follow-on lane for a prepared FLINT-backed QQ Cantor boundary and benchmark 256-bit scalar multiplication against Magma; do not treat this finite-reduction batching lane as completion of Phase 6.
Integrate the Cantor-core prepared finite-field context so torsion and saturation automatically use scalar_batch instead of the reference fallback.
Register test/hyperelliptic-rational-performance.cjs in the shared node-test manifest from the integration lane.
Profile division-box enumeration and add mathematically exact congruence generation if it can beat post-generation filtering.
